## Section 1 — Claude Code host

### Setup

- **Host:** Claude Code (`.claude/agents/`).
- **Dispatch:** host-native subagents via the built-in `Agent` tool.
- **Installed personas:** 4 — see the roster below.

### Team roster (Claude Code)

| Role | `subagent_type` | Hand off… |
|------|-----------------|-----------|
| Scout | `scout` | Codebase exploration, re-seeding, updating `.agents/` docs |
| QA Engineer (Sage) | `qa-engineer` | Analyst slot (AFS production) + Reviewer slot (fresh session) |
| Test Automation Engineer (Axel) | `test-automation-engineer` | Implementer slot — page objects, fixtures, specs, Run Report |
| Test Automation Lead (Tal) | `test-automation-lead` | Pipeline orchestration, merge gate |

Use the `subagent_type` value exactly — it must match a directory name in `.claude/agents/`.

### How to hand off work (Claude Code)

Claude Code has a built-in `Agent` tool. Subagent calls are **synchronous**: you call, the subagent runs to completion, and the result comes back in your next turn. The subagent sees none of your conversation — everything it needs must be in the `prompt`.

**Single subagent:**

    Agent(
      subagent_type="qa-engineer",
      prompt="Analyst slot. Scenario: verify that sale-tagged products show a SALE badge on the product card. Feature file: features/sale-tags.feature. Base URL: https://automationteststore.com/. Framework: Playwright + TypeScript (POM). Produce AFS at test-specs/sale-tags/l1_sale_tag.md. Status: ready-for-automation | blocked | defect-found | un-automatable."
    )

**Parallel subagents — launch in one assistant turn, multiple tool calls:**

    Agent(subagent_type="scout", prompt="Re-scan src/pages/ and update .agents/testing.md with any new page objects. Report changes in under 200 words.")
    Agent(subagent_type="qa-engineer", prompt="Reviewer slot. Review PR #12. Check: assertion strength, selector stability, defect masking, POM discipline. Verdict: APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED with file:line findings.")

Both run concurrently; results arrive on your next turn.

### Anti-patterns

- Don't hand off trivially — one grep and one edit away? Do it.
- Don't hand off to a persona not in the roster above.
- Don't hand off and discard — show the subagent's result in your reply.
- Don't try to simulate async — call, wait, continue.

## Section 2 — GitHub Copilot host

### Setup

- **Host:** GitHub Copilot (`.github/agents/`).
- **Dispatch:** prose-driven `agent` tool invocation.
- **Installed personas:** 6 — see the roster below.

### Team roster (GitHub Copilot)

| Role | Agent file | Hand off… |
|------|------------|-----------|
| Confluence Auth | `confluence-auth` | Confluence authentication setup |
| Create AI Use Case | `create-ai-use-case-confluence` | Publish AI use-case docs to Confluence |
| Epic Automation Coverage | `epic-automation-coverage` | Analyse Jira epics for automation coverage gaps |
| Generate Test Cases | `generate-test-cases` | Generate test case documents from specs or images |
| Git PR | `git-pr` | Open and manage GitHub PRs via GitHub MCP |
| Jira | `jira` | Jira issue management |

### How to hand off work (GitHub Copilot)

Invocation is **prose-driven** — write "Use the `<name>` agent to …" in your response body. The Copilot runtime pattern-matches and dispatches.

**Single subagent:**

> Use the `generate-test-cases` agent to generate test case documents for the sale-tags feature. Context: the spec is at `tests/sale-tags.spec.ts` and the Gherkin is at `features/sale-tags.feature`. Output to `test-cases-output/`.

**Parallel subagents:**

> Use the `jira` agent to fetch open GitHub issues in this repo and list them with titles and priorities.
>
> Use the `git-pr` agent to open a PR from branch `leap_agent` to `main` with the title "feat(tests): add password-reset spec" and description summarising the changes.

### Anti-patterns

- Don't use Claude-style `Agent(subagent_type=…)` calls — Copilot prints them as plain text.
- Don't confuse `handoffs:` (post-run navigation buttons) with mid-run subagent calls.
- Don't hand off to an agent not in the roster above — check frontmatter `agents:` whitelist.
